bull_bear.body: - Capex skewed to owned real estate (rent substitution); FDs on balance sheet generate interest (in other operating income). No buyback/dividend commentary this call. Card notes promoter-stake-consolidation theme (not discussed this call).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Structural circulation decline** — copies down ~2–4%/yr as marginal readers move to digital; management admits "maybe a couple of percentages" market shrinkage.
- **Newsprint inflation** — Q2 to rise further before easing H2; margin hostage to it.
- **Ad cyclicality** — auto weak on macro; education timing-dependent (NEET); reliance on government (DAVP +26% price hike now flowing through).
- **Digital monetization** — years away from being 10–20% of revenue.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, candid, numbers-fluent (Girish handled almost all Q&A). Honest about circulation drift ("we lose some copy, we gain some copy… teams go through frustration") and refusal to give guidance. Deliberately guarded on digital team size (competitive confidentiality).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Print ad growth is an outlier vs broadcasters' soft 1Q — supports the "print resilient in leadership Hindi/Gujarati markets" thesis.
- DAVP (government) +26% rate hike is a quiet tailwind driving double-digit government ad growth.
- Cover price frozen by choice (INR 4.93) — ad growth lets them subsidize readers to defend copies/market share; realization lever intentionally unused.
- Newsprint QoQ (+8%) already at ~INR 53,000; Q2 pain, then H2 relief is the key margin swing factor to verify.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **Print + Digital:** EBITDA INR 1,499 mn (+18%). 250 district editions, ~1,700 news pages/day, ~14,000 stories + 1,800 videos/day across print+digital reporters.
- **Circulation:** ~38 lakh copies (39 lakh Q4, ~40 lakh Q3, 43–44 lakh two years ago). Realization flat; deliberate choice not to hike cover price while ad grows. Market-share gains cited in Rajasthan & MP.
- **Radio (My FM):** 37 stations, +7 planned; revenue INR 425 mn, EBITDA INR 148 mn (+29%), ad +12%; space/time inventory fixed so growth via innovation.
- **Digital:** ~19–20 million MAU (May 2026); #1 Hindi & Gujarati news app; revenue "miniscule," <5% of total, mostly advertising, growing off a small base; monetization is a long-term call, focus still on reader-base build (UP a key market).

latest_quarter.body: - 250 bps margin expansion despite newsprint inflation, via decentralized cost control (travel, admin pushed to all team members, not just HO). Newsprint is the single largest cost and outside management control; everything else is the lever.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue INR 6,220 mn (+8%), EBITDA margin 26.1% (+250 bps), PAT INR 1,007 mn (+25%); ad +10% broad-based (ex education/auto); circulation ~38 lakh, cover price flat INR 4.93; newsprint +13% YoY to ~INR 53k, guided down H2; radio 37 stations (+7 planned), EBITDA +29%; capex FY27 ~INR 150–160 cr; digital ~20m MAU, still <5% revenue.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: education ad recovery post-NEET; newsprint trajectory (Q2 up, H2 down?); circulation copies vs 38 lakh floor; radio station additions & growth; capex pace vs 150–160 cr; UP-election ad build-up._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth:** no formal guidance ("I can't give any guidance… everybody is working hard"). Ad momentum broad-based; education expected to recover in Q2 (NEET shift), so H1 education growth "good."
- **Margin:** no explicit target; drivers = cost saving + top-line, company-wide cost discipline (non-newsprint costs).
- **Newsprint (cost):** +13% YoY / +8% QoQ in Q1 to ~INR 53,000/tonne; expected to **rise further in Q2**, then **start coming down in Q3 and Q4 FY27**.
- **Capex FY27:** ~INR 150–160 crore ("around the same range"), largely buying/building owned property to replace high rentals (e.g. Bhopal).
- **Radio:** 7 more stations lined up (on 37); good bottom-line growth targeted via cost control; ~12% growth described as ambitious/"humongous task."
- Segment-leadership/circulation-promotion spend ~INR 20–25 crore annually.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Digital news apps + AI-generated micro-dramas ("Bhaskar series" based on news, not fiction) — early traction, cross-posted to YouTube; English app later (resources in Hindi/Gujarati).
- UP digital-first expansion ahead of state elections; radio station additions.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Print advertising is doing what most media formats aren't — Q1 ad revenue +10% YoY broad-based across categories (ex-education/auto), driving 250 bps EBITDA-margin expansion to 26.1% and +25% PAT, even as newsprint cost inflated ~13% YoY. The structural story is unchanged: circulation copies keep drifting down (~38 lakh vs ~40 lakh two years ago) with flat realization, so the equity case rests on ad-yield/market-share gains and cost discipline offsetting a slowly shrinking reader base; digital (~20m MAU) remains a long-dated, still-immaterial option.

open.item: Newsprint price to start declining in H2

Operationalise the 14 new radio stations awarded in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's Private FM Radio Phase III auction, of which 7 were launched during FY 2025-26 taking MY FM to 37 cities, leaving the balance still to be commissioned.

Management flags an increase in newsprint prices from supply disruptions, higher raw material costs and forex movements, but anticipates the disruption is temporary and limited to a couple of upcoming months.

Continue sustained investment in high-quality content, user experience, technology capabilities and talent to scale the digital business as a key long-term growth pillar, and build sustainable monetisation opportunities including willingness to pay.
The Company will continue investing in high-quality content, superior user experience, technology capabilities and talent to scale Digital as a key focus area and pillar of long-term growth.

The Company was awarded 14 new radio stations in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting's Private FM Radio Phase III auction, of which 7 were operationalized during FY 2025-26 (no timeline is disclosed for the balance stations).

Newsprint prices increased due to supply disruptions from global geopolitical tensions, higher raw material costs and foreign exchange movements, which the Company anticipates is a temporary disruption for a couple of upcoming months.

The Company will remain focused on disciplined cost management and operational efficiencies to support stable operating performance and healthy margins despite newsprint price volatility, higher raw material costs and foreign exchange movements.
The Company will continue strengthening its integrated "phygital" presence through investments in digital capabilities, technology platforms and high-quality content offerings.
The Company continues its emphasis on circulation growth, reader engagement initiatives and strengthening its market position across core markets.

Management flags that newsprint prices turned upward late in FY 2025-26 on higher raw material and logistics costs, supply constraints and rupee depreciation raising landed import cost, and says it remains watchful of these emerging cost pressures in the coming quarters.

risks.note: Management flags that global geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions, inflationary pressures and commodity-market volatility could hit economic activity and business sentiment, and that any slowdown in economic growth may result in lower advertising expenditure across sectors, thereby affecting industry revenues. Advertising is the company's primary revenue engine, so this is a direct earnings transmission channel rather than a generic macro caveat.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical risk feeding through to advertising spend

risks.note: The newspaper industry remains exposed to fluctuations in newsprint prices, foreign exchange movements and other input costs. Since a significant portion of newsprint requirements is met through imports, adverse movements in global commodity prices or currency exchange rates could impact profitability. The BRSR sourcing disclosure corroborates the structural import dependence: 73.00% of total newsprint was procured from local and national suppliers within India in FY 2025-26 (67.00% in FY 2024-25), leaving the balance sourced internationally.
risks.risk: Input cost volatility — imported newsprint and foreign exchange exposure

risks.note: Rapid technological advancements, changing consumer preferences and increasing dependence on global technology platforms can alter content discovery and consumption patterns. Management specifically flags that the emergence of artificial-intelligence-driven content aggregation and search mechanisms may impact traffic flows and monetisation opportunities for publishers — a structural threat to the digital growth engine the company is investing behind.
risks.risk: Technology and platform disruption, including AI-driven content aggregation

risks.note: The digital media industry continues to face content piracy and unauthorized distribution of content. Weak enforcement of intellectual property rights and rapid proliferation of digital platforms are named as key concerns that can adversely affect monetisation and investments in original content — i.e. it undermines the return on the company's stated heavy spend on original and exclusive content.
risks.risk: Content piracy and weak intellectual property enforcement

risks.note: Management states that such events may adversely affect economic activity, consumer sentiment and advertising expenditure, and explicitly concedes that while the Company continuously monitors developments and maintains appropriate preparedness measures, the impact of such events remains inherently uncertain — an acknowledged unhedgeable tail risk for an ad-funded business.
risks.risk: External and unforeseen events (pandemics, natural disasters, geopolitical conflict)

risks.note: Business continuity is anchored on a single critical system: the SAP system is backed up daily and synced continuously with a Disaster Recovery Server, with a disaster recovery site for SAP at a Mumbai data centre. The company relies on an information security management policy (data protection; email, web and network protection; access control with two-factor authentication; firewall and end-point protection) to prevent data attacks and threats. Disclosed outcome for FY 2025-26: nil data breaches and nil cyber-security consumer complaints.
risks.risk: Cyber-security, data privacy and IT/business-continuity dependence
